findings.evidence: The first layer that has an answer wins.
findings.fix: Name the conflict between layers: when the framework's form and the project's dominant form disagree, follow the project and record the framework exception, because the sentence currently lets the first matching layer win without saying which disagreement to keep.

findings.evidence: RQ workers must import the function's module and jobs can be enqueued by dotted path, so check `job.func_name` in the project's RQ version to see what a queued job holds before assuming the same failure.
findings.fix: Add one Gotchas line: Celery's unregistered-task failure is not assumed for RQ; run the live `job.func_name` check first, and do not rate an RQ rename `contract` until that value shows the queued name.

findings.evidence: Read [references/naming-guidelines.md](references/naming-guidelines.md) when you assign a Priority class, choose a boolean name, decide whether a short or abbreviated name is acceptable, name a symbol with no project convention, or find a convention split across the repo.
findings.fix: Split the trigger by outcome: read the Priority, boolean, abbreviation, fallback-tree or convention-split section only for that case, and do not load the whole file when the Decide row already keeps the name.

findings.evidence: for TypeScript, the project's lint config, the `@typescript-eslint/naming-convention` rule, else a named guide such as the [Google TypeScript style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/tsguide.html)
findings.fix: Make the Google TypeScript style guide the default fallback and name any other guide only as an escape hatch the report must cite.

findings.evidence: No eval asserts the `createdAt` naive-local versus UTC row, the `get`/`find` nullability pairing, or the `tempDir` persistence test.
findings.fix: Add one fixture-backed eval for the time-basis row and one for the tempDir decision, each with an assertion that the naive rename is rejected and the required evidence is cited.

findings.evidence: Non-interactive `makemigrations --noinput` cannot confirm a rename, so it emits RemoveField plus AddField, which drops the column's data.
findings.fix: State the checked boundary: this RemoveField-plus-AddField outcome is Django's non-interactive autodetection, so the report must name Django before applying it and must not treat every ORM rename as data-dropping.

findings.evidence: NestJS string tokens (`@Inject('CONNECTION')`) are matched as strings, so renaming the string breaks injection ([NestJS custom providers](https://docs.nestjs.com/fundamentals/custom-providers)).
findings.fix: Add `checked 2026-11-07` to the NestJS custom-providers link, matching the dated Google and Angular citations.
